title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 315
paragraphs: After this man, the priests listed to me from a papyrus roll the names of three hundred and thirty other kings; and in all these generations of men, eighteen were Ethiopians, one was a woman — a native Egyptian — and the rest were men and of Egyptian race. The name of the woman who reigned was the same as that of the Babylonian queen, namely Nitocris. Of her they said that, desiring to take vengeance for her brother — whom the Egyptians had killed when he was their king and, after killing him, had given his kingdom to her — desiring, I say, to take vengeance for him, she destroyed many of the Egyptians by craft. She had built a very large chamber underground, and making as though she would inaugurate it, but in her mind devising other things, she invited those of the Egyptians whom she knew to have had most part in the murder, and gave a great banquet. Then, while they were feasting, she let the river in upon them by a secret conduit of large size. Of her they told me no more than this, except that when she had accomplished this, she threw herself into a room full of embers in order that she might escape vengeance.
